- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 85+ → 87+), then correct downward with lag.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate sharp downward drifts after peaks.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the “tail” of the price distribution — especially the lowest 5–10% of values — leading to overconfidence in mid-range predictions.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price drops; underestimates downward momentum unless preceded by strong recent decline.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimating sudden drops and overestimating gradual declines.
- Model often misjudges the timing of “recovery” after a dip — tends to predict a rebound too early or too late.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggesting a “U-shaped” bias.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or calendar-driven price patterns (e.g., end-of-month dips, quarterly adjustments).
